generation: P-Series 1st gen (disc, launched Sept 2019 as MY2020, sold to 2023)
identify: Launched Sept 2019 to replace the P2/P3: aero down-tube bottle in its own carrier, top-tube storage, no in-frame storage hatch, 28 mm-class tyres; the 105 build has mechanical TRP Spyre discs and microSHIFT bar-end shifters. The 2024+ P-Series has a trap-door storage hatch under the down tube and takes 34 mm tyres.

cockpit.steerer: Tapered 1-1/8 in (top) to 1-3/8 in (bottom), IS-2 headset, Cervélo carbon P fork (12x100 thru-axle).
cockpit.stem: Standard Cervélo alloy stem, 84 deg (+/-6), 70 mm (48/51), 80 mm (54/56), 90 mm (58/61) per retailer spec of the 105 build; any standard stem can replace it (owners fitted Profile Design, Vision and other stems).
cockpit.stack_system: Stem spacers on an uncut steerer plus aerobar pedestals; Slowtwitch's 2019 test bike came with 30 mm of pedestals and bolts included. Above that, aftermarket riser kits of the fitted aerobar brand.
cockpit.reach_system: Stem length (stock 70-90 mm) is the main reach lever, plus fore-aft pad/bracket positions of the fitted aerobar. Build-dependent: 105 = Zipp Vuka Alumina basebar + extensions (40 cm); Ultegra Di2 = Vision Trimax Carbon base with Metron Si013 armrest hardware, whose armrest brackets can be flipped left-right to point back instead of forward.
cockpit.angle_system: Depends on the fitted aerobar; Zipp Vuka Alumina has armrest tilt shims. No frame-specific tilt system.
cockpit.notes: Because stem, steerer and basebar are standard, most fit changes are a stem/pedestal swap rather than a proprietary part. Fitter-reported limits: stock extensions on the Di2 test bike were too long and too high relative to the pads; one owner's aluminium base/aero bars rotated and had to be bonded after a 70.3; one owner broke the left elbow-pad holder three times in three years at the bar junction. Mechanical front-brake cable routing through integrated stems binds (see incompatible parts).

parts.model: Standard 31.8 mm stem for 1-1/8 in steerer (longer/shorter or different angle)

effect.text: Moves the whole cockpit: a longer stem moves pads forward by roughly the length difference, a positive-rise stem or flipped stem changes height. Stock stems are 70/80/90 mm at 84 deg, so there is room both ways. No maker-stated range.

evidence.says: Spec lists a Cervélo alloy stem 84 deg, 70/80/90 mm by size, on a tapered 1-1/8 to 1-3/8 steerer with IS-2 headset.
Slowtwitch's own P-Series build: a standard, fairly short stem; reviewer adjusted height with pedestals rather than stem spacers.
Owner (Apr 2022) runs a Profile Design stem with a Zipp Vuka basebar on his P-Series.
Another owner build (Apr 2022) uses a Profile Design Aeria Ultimate V2 stem with Vision Trimax Si013 basebar.

parts.needs: Check steerer length above the stem; brake/Di2 routing may need re-running.

effect.text: Replaced the stock aluminium extensions, which were too long and sat too high relative to the pads; cut to the rider's length.

evidence.says: Reviewer cut the stock extensions, found an internal ring then blocked the Di2 bar-end shifter wedge, and switched to TriRig carbon extensions cut to size.

parts.needs: Bar-end shifters need about 20 mm of straight, clear inside diameter at the tip; check before cutting.

effect.text: Owner-fitted replacement aerobar; described as easy to adjust and comfortable. No numbers given.

evidence.says: Di2 P-Series owner (Jan 2022) fitted a 51 Speedshop aerobar setup and TriRig closed-back scoops; warns to watch spacer bolt length.

parts.needs: Correct-length spacer bolts for the chosen stack.

effect.text: Armrest cup swap; changes forearm support, not frame-specific reach/stack.

evidence.says: Same Di2 P-Series owner (Jan 2022) added TriRig closed-back scoops to his 51 Speedshop setup.

effect.text: Full aerobar swap on the standard steerer; owners report it fitted. No reach/stack numbers given.

evidence.says: An owner (Jan 2022) built a P-Series for a friend with a Vision Metron TFA aerobar, without the Snakebite stem.
A second owner (Jan 2022) fitted Metron aerobars with the Snakebite stem; it mounted, but the mechanical front brake cable would not work through it (see incompatible record).

parts.needs: Hydraulic or electronic routing if cables go inside the bar/stem; mechanical cables reported not to fit inside.

parts.model: Metron aerobar / Snakebite stem with internal routing on mechanical-brake builds

effect.text: Mounts, but the brake does not work when the mechanical front cable is routed through the stem and steerer.

parts.reason_incompatible: On mechanical-disc builds (e.g. 105 with TRP Spyre) the front brake cable binds when routed through the Metron/Snakebite stem and steerer, and the Metron bar has too little internal room for mechanical cables and housing. Owners say it works only with hydraulic hose or Di2 wiring.

evidence.says: Owner (Jan 2022): front brake cable bound so much through stem and steerer that the brake would not work; new cables and other routings failed.
A second owner (Mar 2022): little room inside the Metron bars; mechanical cables and outers would not fit, hydraulic/Di2 route was workable.

parts.model: Metron TFE extensions (on Trimax Si013 basebar, PD Aeria Ultimate V2 stem)

effect.text: Full-forearm-support extension swap; no numbers given.

evidence.says: Owner (Apr 2022) built a friend's P-Series with a Profile Design Aeria Ultimate V2 stem, Vision Trimax Si013 basebar and Vision Metron TFE extensions; no problems reported.

effect.text: Aero stem with integrated bottle option, replacing the stock alloy stem; no reach/stack numbers given.

evidence.says: Fitted to a P-Series with Vision Trimax Si013 base bar and Metron TFE extensions (Apr 2022).

effect.text: Integrated stem-and-bar swap; no numbers given.

evidence.says: Owner (Jan 2022) reports his wife's Di2 P-Series runs a TriRig Alpha X with a custom Profile Design Aeria HSF bracket and bottle.

parts.needs: Custom bracket if an Aeria between-the-arms bottle is wanted.

effect.text: Longer forearm support; narrows the space for a between-the-arms bottle cage.

evidence.says: Owner (Jan 2022) fitted Revolver long arm rests; needed a 3D-printed platform for the BTA bottle because the rests narrowed the space.

parts.needs: A raised or narrow BTA bottle platform.

effect.text: Armrest and extension swap on a Zipp Vuka basebar with a Profile Design stem; no numbers given.

evidence.says: Owner (Apr 2022) runs Zipp Vuka bar, Profile Design stem, Kismet arm rests and USE extensions; no problems reported.

gaps: File id uses launch year 2019 (the first P-Series was announced Sept 2019 as model year 2020), not 2020/2021.

No per-size pad stack/reach chart for this generation was found; cervelo.com returned HTTP 429 earlier and was not retried. Slowtwitch fit-thread snippets mention a 58 cm max reach around 525 mm but the post was not opened, so no stock_range is given.

Cockpit spec varies by build and year: 105 = Zipp Vuka Alumina (confirmed); Ultegra Di2 = Vision Trimax Carbon + Metron Si013 hardware (confirmed); Ultegra mechanical and Force eTap AXS cockpits not verified. A used 2020 listing shows a Profile Design basebar, so mid-cycle changes are possible.
Zipp Vuka Alumina and Vision Metron Si riser/spacer kit compatibility on this frame not documented in any source reached.
Owner posts in the P-Series setups thread (2022) do not state the year; they are placed here because only the first generation existed in 2022.
No maker compatibility page names the 1st-gen P-Series specifically; all fits rest on its standard 1-1/8 in steerer and owner reports.
No prices recorded: maker pages not opened.
